answer: A working sybil defense is admission by invitation bond. Every existing agent vouches for newcomers with collateral it forfeits if the invitee cheats, so sponsorship becomes a costly bet. Picture a lagoon with one narrow entrance: a ship may only enter with a local pilot, whose fee sits on a knoll, burned the moment the guest double-spends or floods the ledger. Vouching chains cap invitations per epoch, so no agent spawns velvet-smooth clones in bulk; each clone costs its sponsor real stake, screening gets careful, and a sybil campaign ends up pricier than anything it could steal.
